## Workshops

I run workshops on statistics and computational modelling in psychology, currently covering:

1. [Structural Equation Modelling in Psychology & Social Sciences](https://github.com/GidonFrischkorn/Workshop_SEM) (2-3 days)
2. [Introduction to Bayesian Statistics in R with brms](https://github.com/GidonFrischkorn/Workshop_BayesianStatistics) (1-3 days, depending on depth)
3. [Analyzing Data on the Level of Cognitive Processes / Introduction to the R package bmm](https://github.com/GidonFrischkorn/ws-process-level-data-analysis) (2-3 days)
4. Simulation Studies to challenge intuitions about statistics and psychological theories (2-3 days)

If you are interested in including one of my workshops in your PhD or graduate program, please get in touch.

## Lectures & Seminars

Courses I have taught in undergraduate and graduate programs, most recently:

- **Statistics I** (B.Sc. Psychology, University of Lucerne, autumn 2025), with open [exercise materials](https://unilu-vpf-statistik.github.io/uebung_statistik1/)
- **Statistics IV: Reproducible data analysis in R** (B.Sc. Psychology, University of Lucerne, spring 2026), with interactive [Quarto/webR exercises](https://unilu-vpf-statistik.github.io/uebung_statistik4/)
- **Introduction to Bayesian Statistics** (M.Sc. Psychology, University of Zurich, spring 2024)
- **Using simulations to challenge your intuitions about statistics and cognitive theories** (M.Sc. Psychology, University of Zurich, spring 2022 and 2023)
- **Cutting edge research in human cognition** (M.Sc. Psychology, University of Zurich, autumn 2021)
- **Cognitive Psychology I** (B.Sc. Psychology, University of Zurich, spring 2021, co-taught)

Earlier courses at Heidelberg University covered introductory statistics, psychometrics, and current topics in cognitive psychology. All are weekly sessions with work to be completed between meetings.

## Teaching philosophy

My starting point is that statistical methods carry direct meaning for scientific questions — they are not just mathematical formalism to get through on the way to a result. I cover the mathematical foundations (probability theory, sampling, Bayes' theorem) and connect them to both frequentist and Bayesian analyses, rather than presenting these as separate toolboxes. Students implement analyses in R and learn to read the output in terms of the scientific question they were actually asking.

I also treat reproducibility as part of methods training, not an add-on. Students document their code and data, preregister where appropriate, and share materials on OSF.
